### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/objectql`, touching **48** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/index.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**26** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5d1382a54c04968d7a1c39c1bb51a75c95cf7ea5`.

⛔ **13** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/index.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **7** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **27** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5d1382a54c04968d7a1c39c1bb51a75c95cf7ea5` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `52887fc4c4e6064c1646c586d413a2405b3fb256` — the merge of head `12930e7975217e1e4f66c6eb41fcefd6d888012a` into base `5d1382a54c04968d7a1c39c1bb51a75c95cf7ea5`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 52887fc4c4e6064c1646c586d413a2405b3fb256 && git checkout 52887fc4c4e6064c1646c586d413a2405b3fb256
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 5d1382a54c04968d7a1c39c1bb51a75c95cf7ea5 12930e7975217e1e4f66c6eb41fcefd6d888012a && git checkout -B drift-repro 5d1382a54c04968d7a1c39c1bb51a75c95cf7ea5 && git merge --no-ff 12930e7975217e1e4f66c6eb41fcefd6d888012a

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5d1382a54c04968d7a1c39c1bb51a75c95cf7ea5
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 5d1382a54c04968d7a1c39c1bb51a75c95cf7ea5` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

`Lint · repo & tooling gates` is red on `87d197eb` by sequencing, not by a defect in this diff. `check-adr-anchors` refuses the eight files that cite ADR-0150, because ADR-0150 is not on `main` yet: it is draft PR #31586, which the maintainer approves and merges (Tier H). The order is already set: this PR lands only after #31586 is merged (claim 6724001538). Fix: once #31586 merges, merge `origin/main` into this branch. The citations then resolve and the gate goes green, with no code change. Nothing here is re-run before then.

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT · head 12930e79 · 2026-11-08T21:57Z

Verdict: **ACCEPT** (child R of #31527, built and accepted by the epic seat, ruling 6723571682). Not governed (`check-governed-merges --pr 31637`: `governed: false`). Landing in this stroke: ready, then auto-merge through the queue.

Read: the full diff against `main` (8 files, +1109 / −7), ADR-0150 D3 and D4 as merged in #31586, the dev report 6725151837, and every check run on 12930e79 (all completed; none failed; the skipped ones are UI, docs and opt-in jobs this diff does not reach).

**Red line 1 — never loosens.** `resolvePackageScopedName` has no first-registered fallback. Step 2 refuses two closure candidates (`ambiguous-in-closure`). Step 3 never falls back to an environment-wide answer for a caller with a package (`outside-closure`). Ablations A1–A3 show the pins red with the loosened behaviour put back.

**Red line 2 — ambiguity named.** Every refusal carries every candidate of its step, in `bare-name-one-holder.ts`'s vocabulary plus `{ kind: 'environment' }`. A4 shows the pin red when a candidate is dropped.

**Red line 3 — independently releasable.** No reader imports the resolver. `getItem` has no diff. The three `SchemaRegistry` methods are read-only. `resolveWritePackageScope` keeps its body behind one extracted function (`packageDependencyClosure`), and metadata-protocol's full suite is green on it. The phase-1 parity block pins the resolver to `getItem`'s item for all 11 covered registry types. Readings (a)–(d): (a) phase-1 suites green in CI's Test Core shards; (b) unchanged, no reader wired; (c) no migration; (d) `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` hold: new TypeScript exports only, no schema, protocol, SDK or door change.

**The dev's open question** (a package caller, a name only the environment holds) is ADR-0150 D3 (a) as merged: refuse with `outside-closure`, naming the environment. The PR implements that (option A). No decision is owed.

**Observations, not blocking (carried to the E children):**
- `compositeHoldersOf` scans every key of a type's collection on each call. That is fine with no reader wired. E2, E6 and E8 wire hot readers, and each states its read cost or an index in its PR.
- Like `getItem`, the composite-key parse assumes a package id has no `:`. E2's `(package, objectName, name)` key must not lean on `key.endsWith(':' + name)` alone.
- `PLATFORM_REQUESTED_BARE_NAMES_BY_TYPE` duplicates the CLI's list. Child P (#31669) makes the CLI read objectql's, as the PR notes.

On merge: E1–E8 (#31672–#31675, #31677–#31680) and S1 (#31682) move `pm:blocked` → `pm:queue`.
